messages:
Lina: Heads-up — Horizon asked for a firm commit recommendation for Q3. They want a guaranteed pool that keeps tail latency predictable for bursts. Can we run numbers for committed GPUs + buffer options?
capacity-bot: [autopost] us-west-gpu-pool: 7d avg util 78%, 95p tail 92%. Available spare nodes for burst: 18 GPUs (subject to provisioning lead time).
Marco: Important to know their traffic shape. Is it steady or spiky? spikes will drive headroom more than avg throughput.
Priya: Horizon usage: diurnal with two weekday peaks (US morning, EU afternoon). Median sustained usage ~65 GPUs, peak observed a few times to ~140 GPUs for short windows during experiments. They asked for 120 committed + 20% buffer in their initial ask.
Sam: If peaks hit 140 and they want 120 committed + 20% buffer = 144, that basically means 120 commit + 24 burst. Burst pool 24 may be tricky in us-west during Q3 if other reserves fill. Also consider model variants — switching some traffic to quantized variants (4-bit) reduces throughput requirements ~25-30%.
Lina: Quick sanity calc:
```
# assumptions
peak_target = 140  # peak GPUs needed to meet SLOs
commit_option = 120
buffer_pct = 0.20
buffer_gpus = ceil(commit_option * buffer_pct)  # 24
total_if_buffer = commit_option + buffer_gpus  # 144
avg_gpu_hours_month = 24 * 30  # 720
committed_gpu_hours = commit_option * avg_gpu_hours_month  # 120 * 720 = 86,400
```
So commit 120 => 86.4k GPU-hours/mo. If we push some workload to quantized variants with 30% less GPU time, effective hours drop ~26k.
Aisha: From commercial — horizon wants predictable monthly invoice. If we include 20% burst in the contract we need a premium. Straw pricing: committed-only rate $1.65/GPU-hour, committed+20%burst (guaranteed) $1.90/GPU-hour. On-demand is $2.40/GPU-hour.
Marco: Ops note: current cluster node churn (kube evictions + preemptible pressure) increases risk of transient capacity loss. For guaranteed burst we should reserve nodes on a separate placement group to avoid noisy neighbors. That raises infra cost by ~6%.
Priya: Customer constraint: they need low egress latency from EU too. If we put extra burst capacity in us-west only, EU traffic will see cross-region penalties. They prefer multi-region commit (us-west + eu-west).
Sam: EU A100 inventory is thin in July; our forecasting shows only ~60 GPUs free for new reserved pools in eu-west for the quarter. So multi-region guarantee will force a larger price and potentially a delayed start (2–4 weeks).
Lina: Proposal A (ops-safe): commit 100 GPUs in primary (us-west) + 40% burst policy (up to 40 GPUs) for first 3 months while we observe traffic. Also carve 20 quantized slots to reduce peak GPU-hours. This gives cushion for 140 peaks without multi-region pressure.
Lina: Proposal B (sales-friendly): commit 120 GPUs split 80(us-west)/40(eu-west) + 20% guaranteed burst across regions. Requires eu-west inventory confirmation and a small infra premium.
Aisha: Customer-facing tradeoff: A is faster to provision, lower initial price, but they absorb some cross-region latency. B aligns with their EU latency ask but higher price and slower start. Which do we recommend?
Marco: Ops preference: A, but with an SLA clause — if sustained EU-tail > X for 2 consecutive weeks we'll trigger expansion to eu-west. Also add a canary failover policy to use on-demand in eu-west if reserved can't be provisioned, with automatic traffic throttling.
Priya: Horizon accepted a ramp plan in principle. They want a 90-day review and a 30% cap on sustained burst billing.
Lina: Action items: Priya to send both proposals to Horizon by EOD, Aisha to attach pricing bands, Marco to validate placement group and churn mitigations, Sam to simulate resource hours with quantized split and share projected GPU-hours and cost delta by tomorrow. I'll also schedule a 30-min sync with Horizon's infra lead next week. :calendar:
Aisha: noted — I'll include a draft clause: "burst allowance limited to 30% on average per billing month; excess billed at on-demand" and optional 1-month free burst window for onboarding.
capacity-bot: [forecast snapshot] Q3 projection with Proposal A: expected committed GPU-hours (net) 72,000/mo after quantization adjustments; projected required burst capacity 28 GPUs (peak windows).
